value: visit: yes (ANC province)
finding: KZN was ANC-governed in April 2022, and the President visited (Clermont and other sites) with the Premier. After an IFP-led coalition took over the province in June 2024, no presidential visit was found for the deadly Feb and Mar 2025 KZN floods. All 9 presidential flood visits 2016-2026 were to ANC-governed provinces.

value: anecdotal (1 ward)
finding: Ward 9 (Molweni, a named flood and missing-persons area) changed from DA to ANC in an Oct 2023 by-election, a result attributed to unfixed flood-damaged bridges and roads. There is no systematic study of flood effects on the 2024 vote. The full test is the 4 Nov 2026 local election, for which there is a 2021 ward turnout baseline.
url: data/raw/original_lastmile-data (eThekwini ward baseline, citing Daily Maverick)

value: visit ~5 days after peak
finding: Presidential visit on 13 Apr 2022, not close to an election (the next national election was May 2024). The 2019 Easter-flood visit came about 2 weeks before the May 2019 election.

value: declared on day ~10
finding: National state of disaster declared on 18 Apr 2022. The Auditor-General found the relief response 'too slow': water was not provided quickly enough, owing to lack of preparedness, capacity and project management.

AGSA: 20% of 30 temporary residential units inspected 'were built on unsuitable land as they were close to the riverbank'. In Feb 2025, 5 people died in the Lamontville temporary relocation area that eThekwini built on the Umlazi riverbank. Molweni bridges remained unfixed into 2023.

value: not quantified
finding: Floods 'washed away homes, schools, health centres and critical infrastructure' (Amnesty). No facility count was found in our sources.
not_found
Water supply was cut for days and people used poor-quality water (AGSA). No outbreak figures were found in our sources.

value: 3+ years in temporary housing
finding: 120 mass care centres; the SAHRC called conditions 'worrying and potentially dangerous'. Families were then moved to 14 TEAs, with 1,049 families still there in June 2025 (3+ years). Residents report fear, overcrowding and violence.

value: not counted
finding: Children were among the dead, e.g. the Sokhela family in Clermont lost four children after a church wall collapsed. Residents describe the water arriving at night ('It was 2 in the night, and the water came in'). No count of child deaths was found.
not_found

value: ~3 months (business); 3+ years (housing)
finding: Durban lost an estimated 1.8% of annual GDP, and businesses took about three months to return to pre-flood operations (Presidential Climate Commission). Permanent rehousing was still incomplete in 2025.
Qualitative evidence only: residents in TEAs lost jobs (e.g. domestic workers) because of relocation. No survey figures were found.
The Social Relief of Distress grant was used in major floods, but it requires a municipal 'major incident' declaration. Uptake figures were not found.
not_found in our sources

value: warning issued; radar availability 52% FY22/23
finding: SAWS issued Yellow Level 2 and then Orange Level 8 (Daily Maverick; other sources say Level 5 to 8 to 9). SAWS said its warnings were 'issued in a timely manner' but the rain 'exceeded even the' expectations. SAWS main-radar availability was 52% in FY2022/23.

value: 0 drownings in pilot settlement
finding: The Quarry Road informal settlement (eThekwini/UKZN pilot since 2016: WhatsApp groups, whistles, ropes, evacuation map, ~30 minutes of warning) evacuated with no drownings; one person died by electrocution.
Floods damaged 'communication and electrical systems' (Presidential Climate Commission). No timing data on outages relative to warnings was found.

value: English; 49 of 67 placed deaths at 1-3% English sites
finding: Official warnings were in English. The mayor said the city issued alerts, but residents said none reached them. Of about 67 April-2022 deaths we could place, 49 were at sites where 1-3% of residents speak English as a first language (Census 2011).

value: no cell broadcast
finding: An Emergency Housing Command Centre working with SAWS was created (Apr 2023). There is still no public cell broadcast. The Early Warnings for All roadmap (2025-2029) was launched in Oct 2025. The Presidential Climate Commission recommended strengthening early warning; the Quarry Road model has not been scaled beyond 2-3 pilots.

value: Federal share up to EUR 400m of EUR 800m emergency aid, matched 1:1; EUR 30bn reconstruction fund
finding: The two worst-hit states had premiers from rival parties: NRW under Armin Laschet (CDU, also the CDU/CSU chancellor candidate) and Rhineland-Palatinate under Malu Dreyer (SPD). The federal CDU-SPD government under Merkel ran aid for both on the same formula. Federal emergency aid matched state aid one euro for one euro (up to EUR 400m federal, EUR 800m combined), and the EUR 30bn 'Aufbauhilfe 2021' fund covered all affected states. Merkel visited both states: Schuld (RLP) with Dreyer on 18 July, plus NRW. We found no evidence that party alignment changed aid allocations. Pink and Schmidt (2023) find voters rewarded the parties of their state premiers.

value: Greens +0.4-1.6 pp (DiD); state-premier party up to +6.6 pp; Ahrweiler CDU second vote -12.1 pp
finding: Federal election on 26 Sept 2021, about 10 weeks after the flood. (1) Garside and Zhai 2022 (Research & Politics), difference-in-differences: flood-affected voters were 'marginally (0.4-1.6 percentage points) more likely to vote for the Greens'. Affected voters generally punished the incumbent CDU/CSU, but the CDU appears to have gained in affected parts of NRW. They find no rise in climate issue priority. (2) Pink and Schmidt 2023 (Zeitschrift fuer Politikwissenschaft), using municipal results and satellite damage data: heavily affected voters favoured the party of their state premier by 'up to 6.6 percentage points', with more support for the Greens. (3) Ahrweiler constituency: CDU second-vote share fell from 40.6% (2017) to 28.5% (2021); SPD rose from 22.7% to 28.8%; Greens rose from 6.7% to 12.0%. CDU first vote (Heil) fell from 42.8% to 34.3%. These swings also reflect the national trend and are not isolated flood effects.

value: Visits within 2-4 days; election 73 days after the flood
finding: The flood hit 10 weeks before the 26 Sept 2021 federal election. On 17 July in Erftstadt, Laschet was filmed laughing while President Steinmeier spoke to flood victims. He said: 'It was stupid and shouldn't have happened and I regret it.' Euronews reported the gaffe hit his ratings, and Olesen (2024) links the images to his collapse from front-runner and the CDU defeat. Merkel toured Schuld with Dreyer on 18 July, calling the scene 'surreal, ghostly'. Finance Minister Scholz (SPD candidate, later chancellor) announced the aid package.

value: EUR 800m emergency; EUR 30bn fund; about EUR 6.2bn (about 21%) paid after 5 years
finding: The declarations were local. Altenahr's state of emergency and evacuation order (50 m either side of the Ahr) came at 23:09 on 14 July, when the water was already dangerously high. Funding: (a) Cabinet emergency aid on 21 July 2021, one week after the flood: up to EUR 400m federal, matched 1:1 by the states. (b) RLP 'Soforthilfe' for households in Ahrweiler district: about 17,100 applications, over 12,300 approved, EUR 24.5m paid (about EUR 1,992 each on average), with 'durchschnittliche Bearbeitungsdauer ... zwei Tagen' (average two days to payment), status 10 Sept 2021. (c) The Bundestag approved the EUR 30bn 'Aufbauhilfe 2021' fund on 7 Sept 2021, about 15 billion of it for RLP. By 30 June 2026 only about EUR 6.2bn had been paid out, 'gut einem Fuenftel' (just over a fifth) of the fund (ZDF, 14 July 2026). RLP 2.5bn, NRW 2.6bn; about EUR 2.4bn paid in the Ahr valley against about EUR 3.72bn approved. (d) EU Solidarity Fund: over EUR 612m for Germany (Dec 2022).

value: 62/112 Ahr bridges destroyed; rail fully restored after 4.4 years
finding: 'Of the 112 bridges in the flooded 40 km of the Ahr valley (Rhineland-Palatinate), 62 bridges were destroyed.' The Ahr Valley Railway reopened in phases from Nov 2021 and fully on 14 Dec 2025, after a EUR 590m rebuild (22 bridges, 5 tunnels, 10 stations). As of July 2026, several municipal bridges (e.g. Bachemer and Landgrafenbruecke) are due only at end-2026. Are-Gymnasium: 880 students still in containers, completion expected end-2027. Political fallout came from the warning and response failures, not the repair pace. RLP Interior Minister Lewentz resigned (Oct 2022), and Anne Spiegel resigned as federal family minister (Apr 2022). Victims have complained about slow aid payment.

value: about 180 GP practices; about 68 NRW hospitals affected; Bad Neuenahr hospital closed about 4 weeks
finding: NHESS critical-infrastructure note: 'An estimated 180 general-practitioner practices have been affected' in Germany and 'Approximately 68 hospitals have been affected' in NRW, several needing at least 1.5 years to rebuild. Krankenhaus Maria Hilf in Bad Neuenahr was cut off on the flood night ('Die Situation glich einem Blackout', the situation was like a blackout). It 'war ... fast einen Monat lang geschlossen' (was closed for almost a month) and reopened about four weeks after the flood. Also 19 daycare centres and 17 schools were damaged in RLP, affecting more than 8,000 students.

We found no study of births or pregnancy outcomes after the 2021 German floods. The only item is an anecdote: in 2026 Dernau's mayor spoke of a 'regelrechten Babyboom' (a real baby boom) in the village (ZDF). It is not evidence of a flood effect.

value: No outbreak documented
finding: We found no documented outbreak. The ECDC rapid risk assessment rated the risk very low/low for tetanus and hepatitis A, and intermediate/high for SARS-CoV-2, E. coli, Salmonella, Cryptosporidium and norovirus. Drinking water: chlorination and an urgent boil-water advisory across Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler, Altenahr and Adenau. Mobile tetanus vaccination was provided. The head of the public-health physicians' association said there were signs of diarrhoeal illness 'aber zum Glueck nicht auf echte Seuchen' (but luckily no real epidemics). Aerztezeitung headline: 'Keine Seuchengefahr mehr im Flutgebiet' (no more epidemic risk in the flood area).

value: PTSD 28.2% at 1 year; 14.4% still displaced at 1 year
finding: At least 17,000 people in the Ahr valley lost homes or had considerable damage. Among survey respondents one year on (n=516, 411 usable), over 40% had to vacate, 14.4% still could not return, and 90% had not fully repaired. PTSD: '28.2 %' showed PTSD indications about one year after the flood, 36% of women against 22% of men (NHESS 2024). Older adults (65+) three years after: 47% anxiety, 38% depression, 39% PTSD (ScienceDirect 2025). Temporary housing included 25 tiny houses in Grafschaft for about 100 people. Some residents were still rebuilding five years later.

value: 3 children among Ahr dead; youngest aged 4; night-time peak 01:00-02:00
finding: AP via Gulf News: 'The oldest victim was 97, the youngest was 4. Most of those killed were over 60, but three children, 12 residents of an assisted living facility and a volunteer firefighter were also among the dead.' Timing: a weekday night (Wednesday 14 to Thursday 15 July, during school summer holidays in RLP). The peak in the deadliest areas was around 01:00-02:00, so most people were at home and many were asleep.

value: Price declines only in nearby or high-climate-belief flood zones (magnitude not retrieved)
finding: Gruhl, Brehm, Ghosh, Breidenbach and aus dem Moore (2025), 'Adjusting to the New Normal: River Flood Risk and the Real Estate Market', Environmental & Resource Economics 88(9). A hedonic difference-in-differences study using the July 2021 flood as a shock. Flood-prone areas near the flood, or with stronger climate-change beliefs, saw house price declines; other flood risk zones showed no significant effect. We could not access the size of the effect.

value: about 21% of fund paid at 5 years; >1,000 homes fully rebuilt (RLP, 2026)
finding: We found no night-lights study of the Ahr. Rebuild indicators: power was about 50% restored within two days, and no emergency generators were needed after eight weeks (NHESS 2022). RLP state portal (1 July 2026): about 20,800 complete aid applications, over 20,000 approved, EUR 3.72bn approved, and 'Ueber 1.000 Wohngebaeude' (over 1,000 homes) fully rebuilt. Only about a fifth of the EUR 30bn fund had been paid after five years. Some schools, Kitas and bridges are still due in 2026-2027.

value: Flood-hit neighbourhoods 3% (about EUR 1,500) poorer; job loss not quantified
finding: Odersky and Loeffler (IZA DP 16540 / J. Economic Inequality): 'Average household income is around 1,500 euros or three percent lower in flood-affected neighborhoods than in non-affected neighborhoods nearby', meaning poorer households were more exposed. The main local sectors, viticulture and tourism, were hit hard, with over 38 wineries losing facilities and stock. We found no study quantifying job or income loss. The labour agency reports Ahrweiler unemployment at 4.1% in May 2026, with no flood attribution.

value: 12,300 Soforthilfe payments; 18,140 reconstruction applications; EUR 1.5bn approved (ISB)
finding: Soforthilfe in Ahrweiler district: about 17,100 applications (about 4,100 duplicates), over 12,300 approved, about 580 rejected, EUR 24.5m paid by 10 Sept 2021. Aufbauhilfe (ISB RLP, deadline 30 June 2026, extended from 2023): 18,140 complete applications and EUR 1.5bn approved. Household contents: 12,006 approved, EUR 146m. Private buildings: 4,045 approved, EUR 682m. Businesses: 819 approved, EUR 698m. 713 rejected. About EUR 14bn was earmarked for the Ahr valley. Private households got up to 80% of damage covered, up to 100% in hardship cases.

value: about 25% insured; 37% RLP coverage before (59% by 2025)
finding: The insured loss of EUR 8.2bn (GDV) was about 25% of the EUR 33bn economic loss. Only 37% of RLP homes had natural-hazard (Elementar) cover before the flood, rising to 59% by end-2025. The state fund covered uninsured owners at 80% of damage (up to 100% in hardship cases), with insurance payouts deducted. The subsidy was reduced to 90% for insurable property where no cover was later taken out. In the PTSD survey, 10.1% said their insurer did not acknowledge the damage or pay.

value: Warning lead about 13 h; gauge destroyed; only 17.5% got evacuation instructions
finding: Forecasts were good; getting them to people failed. EFAS sent a first informal notice on 10 July and more than 25 warnings for Rhine/Meuse regions by 14 July. The ECMWF Extreme Forecast Index flagged the event on 12 July, and DWD issued heavy-rain warnings on 13 July. RLP's LfU issued ten forecasts for Altenahr on 14 July, and at 19:35 forecast a level above 5 m. The Altenahr gauge was destroyed at 332 m3/s, above the 236 m3/s record, so real-time observation was lost. Hannah Cloke (EFAS co-designer) called it 'a monumental failure of the system'. The first warning came about 13 h before the upstream peak, but only 17.5% of those affected got a warning with evacuation instructions (NHESS 2025).

value: 29% (RLP) and 35% (NRW) got no warning; 85% of those warned did not expect severe flooding
finding: Survey of 1,315 residents: '35 % of the respondents from NW and 29 % from RP did not receive any warning'. Of those warned, '85 % did not expect very severe flooding', and 46% lacked knowledge of protective behaviour. About 20% in Ahrweiler got a KATWARN warning. Many survivors heard from family and neighbours instead. Ahrweiler district issued a KATWARN warning in the early afternoon of 14 July, but the district-level disaster declaration and evacuation came around 23:00.

value: about 200,000 without power; mobile disruption across all severely affected areas
finding: 'At the peak of the event, around 200 000 people experienced power outages in Germany.' 'In Germany, all severely affected areas experienced disruption of mobile network services' (NHESS 2022). The 1,300 initial 'missing' reports were largely due to downed mobile networks. Warning chains failed partly because digital broadcasting, mobile and radio all depended on electricity. Some NINA warnings arrived late. Deutsche Telekom reported great damage to infrastructure in the Ahr valley and Eifel.

value: 12 disabled care-home residents died; 16% of victims disabled; about 80% aged 60+
finding: Disability: 12 residents with severe disabilities drowned on the ground floor of a Lebenshilfe home in Sinzig, where one night carer was responsible for both houses. 16% of Ahr victims had disabilities (7 with mobility impairments, 14 with cognitive impairments), and 78-80% were over 60 (NHESS 2025). Language: a study of older adults found 'persistent language barriers, especially for older adults with migrant backgrounds' limiting access to information. Warnings were app- and German-language based. We found no study specifically on deaf or blind access to warnings in 2021.

value: Cell broadcast live Feb 2023; EUR 88m sirens; new RLP disaster agency 2025
finding: (1) Cell Broadcast: announced Aug 2021, telecoms law amended, first national test on Warntag 8 Dec 2022, regular operation from Feb 2023. (2) Siren programme 1.0: EUR 88m (up to EUR 86m for states in 2021-22, EUR 2m for MoWaS control), later a EUR 30m 'Sirenenfoerderprogramm 2.0'. (3) RLP: new State Office for Fire and Disaster Protection (Koblenz) from 1 Jan 2025. A new fire and disaster protection law requires municipal alarm and response plans, regular exercises, a full-time inspector in each district and a 'Voralarm' (pre-alarm).

value: Direct provincial grants: Sindh Rs15bn, Balochistan Rs10bn; KP/GB routed via NDMA instead
finding: Relief flows were visibly politicised along federal (PDM coalition led by PML-N, with PPP) vs PTI-run provinces (KP, and Punjab at the time) lines. Pakistan Today (15 Sep 2022) reported the Finance Ministry began transferring "Rs15 billion to Sindh and Rs10 billion to Balochistan in the head of flood grants", while "in the case of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan, it would be disbursed to flood affectee through federal government's departments like the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)" (headline: 'Centre playing politics with grants release to KP, GB flood affectees'; based on unnamed finance-division sources). In parallel, PTI ran its own telethon (29 Aug 2022, >Rs5bn pledged), with money routed to "the official accounts of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab governments"; Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal questioned it. Imran Khan kept holding rallies ('Rallies will be held in floods, even wars'), which the government criticised.

value: PPP 84 general Sindh Assembly seats (2024), its best result since 2008
finding: No systematic study found linking 2022 flood exposure to Feb 2024 results. Descriptively, the PPP (governing Sindh, the worst-hit province) faced "criticism of his party's governance of Sindh for the past four terms, especially after cataclysmic 2022 flooding, which destroyed much of the province" (Al Jazeera), yet won a record 84 general seats in the Sindh Assembly on 8 Feb 2024. Flood housing (2.1 million houses with ownership rights) featured in Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's campaign. No evidence of an electoral penalty for the incumbent in flood-hit Sindh.

value: First PM visit 31 Jul 2022; by-polls postponed Sep 2022; general election Feb 2024
finding: PM Shehbaz Sharif visited flood-hit Jhal Magsi (Nasirabad division, Balochistan) on 31 July 2022, promising "Rs1 million to families of each victim" from federal and provincial governments each; later visited Sukkur and Jaffarabad (Rs10bn grant for Balochistan) and did aerial surveys of Sindh/Balochistan. UN Secretary-General Guterres visited Sukkur, Usta Muhammad, Mohenjo-Daro and Karachi on 9-10 Sep 2022. Elections were disrupted: the ECP decided to "indefinitely postpone the by-elections in at least 10 National Assembly constituencies and three provincial assembly seats" scheduled 11 Sep-2 Oct 2022, citing "floods and the unavailability of military and paramilitary personnel"; the Sindh local-government second phase (Karachi/Hyderabad divisions) was postponed repeatedly from July/August 2022 due to rain and floods. The general election was held 8 Feb 2024, about 18 months after the floods.

value: BISP Rs66.6bn to 2.66m families by 25 Oct 2022; Geneva pledges ~US$10bn, ~87-90% loans
finding: Federal government declared a national emergency on 25 Aug 2022 and deployed the military. Federal cash relief: BISP Flood Relief Cash Assistance, Rs25,000 per family, target Rs70bn for 2.7 million families; by 25 Oct 2022 BISP had paid "66,585,950,000 among 2,663,438 flood-affected families" (~97.3%) -- i.e. most paid within ~2 months. UN flash appeal revised to US$816m (UNICEF share US$173.5m, only 13% funded as of 7 Oct 2022). Geneva conference (9 Jan 2023) raised about US$10-10.9bn in pledges (Express Tribune reported $10.7bn), but Dawn reported "$8.7bn are loans" with ~$1.3bn grants; Islamic Relief said a year later "Almost 90% of the pledges came in the form of long-term loans" and most had not reached people.

value: Transport damage USD 3.3bn; 13,115 km roads, 439 bridges damaged; 40 'ghost' bridges in Upper Dir
finding: PDNA: Transport and Communications damage USD 3.3 billion (third-largest sector). About 13,115 km of roads and 439 bridges damaged (Wikipedia compilation of NDMA data). Accountability case: an investigation into the 2022 flood relief fund in Upper Dir (KP) found rampant embezzlement, with 40 approved steel bridges never built (Express Tribune, 'Flood relief scandal: 40 bridges never built'). No systematic data found on % of roads/bridges repaired.

value: >1,460 health facilities damaged (~10% nationally)
finding: "Over 1460 healthcare facilities have been damaged in Pakistan since June" 2022 (Alied et al., Annals of Medicine and Surgery, 2023). UNFPA (30 Aug 2022): over 1,000 health facilities partially or fully damaged in Sindh and 198 in affected Balochistan districts. WHO reported ~10% of health facilities nationally damaged or destroyed (Oct 2022, cited by East Asia Forum). PDNA health-sector damage estimated at about USD 109 million.

value: ~650,000 pregnant women affected; 73,000 births expected within a month
finding: UNFPA (30 Aug 2022): "almost 650,000 pregnant women in the flood-affected areas require maternal" health services; "Up to 73,000 women expected to deliver next month will need skilled birth" attendants and newborn care. UNFPA (21 Sep 2022): "Nearly 130,000 pregnant women in need of urgent health services", "more than 42,000 of whom are due to give birth in the next three months". No population-level data found on actual birth outcomes (stillbirth, low birth weight, maternal deaths) attributable to the floods.

value: >540,000 malaria cases (Jul-Oct 2022); 25,932 dengue cases; ~534,800 diarrhoea treatments in Sindh camps
finding: Malaria: WHO/UN reported over 540,000 malaria cases July-early Oct 2022 in flood-affected areas; Sindh August cases rose from 19,826 (Aug 2021) to 69,123 (Aug 2022) and high-burden districts from 178,657 (Aug 2022) to 389,372 (Sep 2022) (Tabassum et al., Health Science Reports 2023). Dengue: 25,932 confirmed cases and 62 deaths nationally 1 Jan-27 Sep 2022 (WHO DON414). Diarrhoea/skin: "534 800" people treated for diarrhoea and "594 241" for skin illnesses at Sindh medical camps (Alied et al. 2023). Cholera and typhoid also reported. WHO warned of a 'second disaster'.

value: 7.9m displaced; ~598k in camps; 1.3m still displaced >1 year later
finding: 7.9 million displaced, of whom ~598,000 were in relief camps (OCHA, 23 Sep 2022). More than a year later IOM reported over 1.3 million people still displaced in the 30 worst-affected districts. An IGC survey of 5,100 rural Sindh households found "Only 41% of households evacuated", floods lasted on average 74 days with 24 days of displacement, and 56% stayed to guard house/land. Mental health: a Hyderabad (Sindh) study reported depression 68%, anxiety 62%, PTSD 55% among flood-affected respondents (International Journal of Asian Education and Psychology; small non-representative sample); Islamic Relief (Jan 2024) quoted a Sindh villager: "five people have committed suicide in the past year".

value: 615-647 children dead (~35-37% of all deaths)
finding: UNICEF (Oct 2022): "Pakistan's catastrophic floods have already claimed the lives of 615 children" (615 children killed 14 Jun-28 Sep; 4,006 injured). Early September reporting (CNN, 4 Sep 2022) said about a third of the ~1,280 dead were children; Avoidable Deaths Network: "children account for over a third of total deaths". Final NDMA count commonly cited as 647 children of ~1,739 deaths (~37%). Children also faced follow-on risks: UNICEF estimated over half a million children with severe acute malnutrition; later screening found >1 in 9 children in flood areas with SAM.
No study or official data found on land or property value changes in flood-affected areas after the 2022 floods.

value: Night lights recovered ~10 weeks after flooding; ~5% of 2.1m damaged homes fully rebuilt by Jan 2024
finding: Night lights: a NASA Black Marble study of the Indus flood found radiance in flooded areas was affected for ~13 weeks, fell by a factor of ~5 at the main flood, and took ~10 weeks after flooding to recover to pre-flood levels, with uneven recovery across socio-economic groups (ESS Open Archive preprint). Housing: Islamic Relief (Jan 2024) found "only around 5% of flood-damaged homes rebuilt" a year after Geneva. Sindh People's Housing for Flood Affectees (2.1m-house programme): by June 2024 over 100,000 houses completed and 525,000 under construction (Dawn); Amnesty (Oct 2024) cites 100,000 completed and 500,000 under construction. World Bank says its Sindh housing project supported over 410,000 core housing units.

value: 4.3m workers affected; 8.4-9.1m pushed into poverty; GDP -2.2%
finding: PDNA: "A total of 4.3 million workers across all provinces have been affected"; agriculture and livestock damage USD 3.7 billion; GDP loss "around 2.2 percent of FY22 GDP"; national poverty could rise 3.7-4.0 percentage points, "pushing between 8.4 and 9.1 million more people below the poverty line". ILO (28 Sep 2022): "2.36 to 3.6 million jobs may have been lost and/or disrupted". Satellite assessment of Sindh: expected production losses of 88% for cotton, 80% for rice, 61% for sugarcane; combined crop and livestock loss ~USD 1.7bn in Sindh. PDNA notes women lost agricultural/livestock livelihoods.

value: 2.66m families paid Rs25,000 (97.3% of target) within ~2 months
finding: BISP flood cash (Rs25,000/family) reached 2,663,438 families (Rs66.59bn, 97.3% of Rs70bn target) by 25 Oct 2022; Sindh 1,820,504 families, Punjab 325,432, KP 302,454, Balochistan 214,582, GB 466. Coverage limits: Humanitarian Outcomes reported that only 2.76 million of the over 8 million existing BISP beneficiary families living in flood-affected areas received payments, and the programme did not cover people newly impoverished by the floods. Sindh housing programme: ~1.02 million families had received financial support by Aug 2025 (reported by UrduPoint).

value: Insured share ~0% of ~US$15bn direct losses
finding: Munich Re NatCatSERVICE: "Direct losses are estimated to be at least US$ 15bn" and "Almost nothing was insured". Pakistan's insurance penetration is about 1% and crop insurance has little reach (Express Tribune commentary). No study found comparing recovery of insured vs uninsured households.

value: Extreme rain predictable ~6 days ahead; ~4 operational PMD radars
finding: Forecast skill was good at the meteorological level: Malik et al. (Environmental Research: Climate, 2023) found "the extreme precipitation during 17-18 August 2022 was predictable a week before the event"; all models captured it at a 6-day lead time, with UKMO/ECMWF hit rates above 0.5 up to 5 days ahead. ECMWF reported signals of severe flooding up to 3 weeks ahead in extended-range forecasts. Observation gaps: PMD runs only a few weather radars (Islamabad, Karachi, Mardan, Sialkot as of 2026, with Multan being added with JICA support) (radar ranges: S-band ~450 km, X-band Mardan ~120 km, C-band Sialkot ~350 km; INP, 2026); weak mountain monitoring and slow data sharing between provinces were also reported.

value: 'Zero effective lead time'; 41% of surveyed Sindh households evacuated
finding: Last-mile warning was weak. UNESCO review: communities experienced "zero effective lead time" in 2022 (and 2025) even when forecasts existed, and recommended impact-based forecasting, local 'human sensors', sirens, mosque loudspeakers and radio. A Frontiers in Earth Science (2023) review of Pakistan's flood EWS found "77% of respondents saw a lack of coordination between producers and consumers as a significant obstacle", that many at risk did not take warnings seriously, and that "Nearly 90% of the project budget is allocated" to monitoring/warning technology rather than community components. IGC survey in rural Sindh: "Only 41% of households evacuated", many staying to guard land (76% lacked a formal title deed), so warnings alone would not have moved people.

value: 10 Balochistan districts lost phone/internet on 26 Aug 2022
finding: On 26 Aug 2022 telephone and internet services were cut in 10 Balochistan districts (Quetta, Ziarat, Khuzdar, Loralai, Pishin, Chaman, Panjgur, Zhob, Qila Saifullah, Qila Abdullah) after the PTA cited "a serious damage to the cable and optical-fibre network due to torrential rains and flash floods"; PTCL fibre was cut in three places; services were partly restored within hours via bypass and satellite links. The Nation reported internet services suspended in 80% of Balochistan (31 Aug 2022). UNESCO notes GSM, electricity and internet "frequently fail during severe weather events", limiting SMS alerts.

No 2022-specific evidence found on which languages (Urdu/English vs Sindhi, Balochi, Saraiki, Pashto) warnings were issued in, or on reach among non-Urdu speakers. General evidence on Pakistan's EWS (Frontiers 2023, citing Shah et al. 2022): "Official early warning system uses technical language, making it harder for at-risk populations to comprehend", and women are excluded or only partly included in preparedness activities. UNESCO recommends warnings be "translated into localized and actionable guidance for communities".

value: NEOC revamped (2024); 4RF (Dec 2022); new radar under installation
finding: Post-2022 changes: the Resilient Recovery, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Framework (4RF, launched 21 Dec 2022; US$16.26bn of interventions) set out the recovery and resilience plan; NDMA revamped its National Emergencies Operation Centre (NEOC), which PM Shehbaz Sharif visited on 21 Jun 2024, with "multiple satellite feeds, software and artificial intelligence tools" and a claimed "capability to forecast weather six to ten months in advance"; NDMA launched a disaster-alert mobile app (Pak NDMA Disaster Alert); PMD is adding radars (Multan, JICA-supported). No independent evaluation found showing improved last-mile warning; the UNESCO review says 'zero effective lead time' recurred in 2025.

value: Qualitative evidence of partisan contestation over reconstruction funds and alleged politicised food aid; no quantified aid-by-alignment estimate
finding: Beira (Sofala capital) was governed by the opposition MDM (mayor Daviz Simango) while the national and provincial governments were FRELIMO. Schubert (2024, Buildings & Cities) reports 'the municipal and the national government were jockeying for money and influence in the reconstruction process' and that residents accused FRELIMO of trying to economically 'strangle' the opposition-run city; reconstruction was centralised in a national office (GREPOC) supervised by the Minister of Public Works (PDNA). International IDEA (Rosario 2022) states that in resettlement/accommodation centres 'The distribution of supplies in these centres also became a political tool' and 'queuing for food assistance ... became a way to garner or buy votes for those who held power in the state administration'. The Beira Municipal plan in the PDNA notes 'The Beira Municipality has very few resources' and appeals to national government and donors. No quantitative study of aid allocation by party alignment found.

value: Sofala abstention 49.61% (2014) -> 42.39% (2019); Sofala registration 79.92% of target; FRELIMO won all provinces/all 161 districts; national FRELIMO ~71%, Nyusi ~73%
finding: The 15 October 2019 general election (7 months after Idai) was held without postponement beyond a 15-day delay to voter registration (Council of Ministers, 26 March 2019). International IDEA case study (Rosario, 2022): 'over 160,000 people forced to shelter in 164 collective, temporary accommodation centres ... lost their identity documents, which are required to register to vote'; voter registration in Sofala reached only 79.92% of target (1,028,374 of 1,286,737) and Manica 83.98%. Yet abstention FELL in cyclone provinces: Sofala 49.61% (2014) -> 42.39% (2019); Manica 54.00% -> 39.28%. FRELIMO won every province including Sofala, 'where RENAMO had nearly always received a majority', and 'received the most votes in all 161 districts of Mozambique, which had never happened before'. IDEA concludes: 'The cyclones undoubtedly benefited the ruling party and had a direct impact on electoral performance, in particular of the opposition parties', while also noting 'there is no direct or obvious causal relationship' and that 'most of the accommodation centres were set up to house people in their original constituencies, so the electoral results ... were not significantly affected.' No econometric study isolating Idai's effect was found. RENAMO and MDM rejected the results alleging fraud.

value: Presidential flyover ~18 March 2019; Cabinet in Beira 19 March; election 15 October 2019 (~7 months later)
finding: President Nyusi made an aerial survey within days: 'Waters from the rivers Pungue and Buzi have broken their banks, wiping out entire villages, isolating communities and we could see, as we flew above, bodies floating' and 'everything indicates that we can have a record of more than 1,000 dead' (18 March 2019). He chaired a Cabinet meeting in Beira on 19 March, declaring a national emergency and three days of national mourning from 20 March. Nyusi also met Beira's MDM mayor Daviz Simango in Beira (Club of Mozambique). Timeline: landfall 14 March; registration postponement 26 March; registration 15 April-30 May; campaign 31 August-12 October; election 15 October 2019 (IDEA Table 3). IDEA: the ruling party, 'accompanied by the state military apparatus, was able to enter areas affected by the cyclones ... that were inaccessible to the opposition parties'; opposition said 'people are always in meetings organized by administration officials ... the food assistance is forcing people to be in meetings all the time.'

value: Emergency declared 19 Mar 2019 (5 days after landfall); pledges USD 1.2 bn vs needs USD 3.2 bn; USD 704 m spent by Aug 2024 (56% of programme)
finding: PDNA: Government 'Declared a National Sate of Emergency on 19th March 2019', established the post-Cyclone Idai Recovery Program (PREPOC) on 26 March and the Post-Cyclone Reconstruction Office (Decree 26/2019, 11 April 2019). UN international appeal: USD 281.7 million. Beira International Pledging Conference (31 May-1 June 2019) mobilised pledges of USD 1.2 billion against PDNA needs of USD 3.2 billion (Idai + Kenneth). By 21 August 2024 the government reported USD 704 million spent, '56 percent compliance' with PREPOC, and USD 526.77 million 'to be spent by 2026' (govt spokesperson Filimao Suaze). Fiscal note: PDNA says total needs 'represent around 22% of the country's GDP'. No automatic declaration threshold (e.g., % of GDP or deaths) found.

value: 56% of PREPOC by Aug 2024; >90% of damaged infrastructure by Nov 2025 (govt claim)
finding: PDNA damage: 3,490 km national roads (29% of total), 20 bridges, 1,345 km transmission lines, 10,216 km distribution lines, 30 substations, ~4,000 transformers, 4,219 classrooms. Government progress reports: by Aug 2024, 5,750 new homes, 3,269 of 4,745 classrooms, 4,154 km road and 28 bridges, 1,066 of 1,352 km transmission lines restored (Club of Mozambique); by Nov 2025 AIM reported 'more than 90 per cent' of Idai-damaged infrastructure rebuilt, incl. 11,457 homes and 3,514 classrooms. Fallout: Schubert (2024) found four years on 'very limited visible results' and a common refrain that 'All the money for Idai reconstruction has been stolen'; Beira residents of Ndunda chased away GREPOC technicians in 2023 (Integrity Magazine). PDNA promised 'independent annual audit' of programme resources; no published audit or prosecutions found.

value: 89 partially + 3 completely destroyed health facilities (PDNA); services recovered within ~3 months
finding: PDNA: '89 health facilities partially destroyed', '3 health facilities completely destroyed', '2 health training facilities were partially destroyed'; health damage USD 81.5 m and losses USD 108.9 m; 'a 50% decrease in HIV consultations'. Peer-reviewed ITS study (Global Health: Science and Practice, PMC9476482): '90 health facilities and 3,145 health workers' homes' damaged; first antenatal visits fell 23% and measles vaccinations 25% in March 2019; 'within 3 months post-cyclone, almost all districts recovered to pre-Idai levels'. WHO AFRO: 'More than 50 health facilities across Sofala Province ... suffered serious damage', including Buzi District Hospital (89 beds). Government reported 36 health units rehabilitated and 54 under reconstruction by Nov 2025 (AIM).

value: 75,000 pregnant women affected; ANC first visits -23% in March 2019; institutional deliveries ~-20% in highly affected districts
finding: PDNA/UNFPA: '75,000 pregnant women among the affected, and 45,000 live births are expected in the next 6 months', '7,000 of those could experience life-threatening complications'; 'Almost 8,000 pregnant women affected by the cyclone are HIV+'; '83,000 affected women are lactating'. ITS study (PMC9476482): first ANC visits declined 23% (95% CI 0.62-0.96) in March 2019 and institutional deliveries showed a ~20% relative loss in highly affected districts, recovering within 3 months; Buzi showed a rebound (+22% ANC) by May. No study of birth weight, preterm birth or maternal deaths attributable to Idai found.

value: ~6,768 suspected cholera cases, ~8 deaths (CFR 0.12%); ~803,000 vaccinated (98.6% coverage) within ~3 weeks of landfall
finding: Cholera outbreak declared 27 March 2019 in Sofala; first acute diarrhoea cases reported 27 March and 'Within approximately a week, 1,428 suspected cholera cases were reported' (PMC6838597). WHO (5 April): 'more than 2430 cases and 3 deaths'. PDNA: '6,627 cases of cholera reported thus far'. Final tallies reported in the literature: 6,768 suspected cases by 21 April 2019, CFR 0.12% (~8 deaths), concentrated in Beira, Dondo, Nhamatanda and Buzi (Infectious Diseases of Poverty 2020). OCV: 'almost 900 000 doses' arrived in Beira on 2 April (WHO/UNICEF, Gavi-funded); six-day campaign reached >800,000 people in four districts (803,125; 98.6% of target). UNICEF: 'Five hundred beds in seven cholera treatment centres'. Malaria also surged: 14,863 cases per PDNA; WHO/OCHA reported 26,787 cases in Sofala by 9 May.

value: 400,000 displaced; ~88,000 resettled in 66 sites; >100,000 still in temporary shelter at 1 year; mental-health prevalence not measured
finding: 400,000 displaced; 160,927 in 164 temporary accommodation centres (PDNA, end April). Jacobs & Almeida (Refugee Survey Quarterly, 2020): 'the government resettled around 88,000 individuals from affected areas to new sites' and 'INGC ... created 66 resettlement sites'; in November 2019 people were 'still living in the tents' and 'Many others were still struggling to find new livelihoods and continued to depend on aid'. IOM DTM (Dec 2019): 93,516 people in 76 resettlement sites. Oxfam (March 2020): 'over 100,000 people in Mozambique are still living in temporary shelters'. PDNA: 49% of assessed locations reported increased personal-safety concerns; 'At least 7,000 women in reproductive age are at risk of suffering rape'. Mental health: no Mozambique prevalence survey found; Beira psychiatrist Vasco Cumbe: 'what we know of the prevalence of common mental illness in general is very limited' (Mail & Guardian, 2026).

value: not_found (children share of deaths); landfall at night 14-15 March, main flood killing 16-17 March
finding: No age-disaggregated death count for Mozambique found. Timing: landfall 'on the night of 14 to 15 March' (PDNA), followed by river flooding 16-17 March that submerged Buzi district; Nyusi saw 'bodies floating' from the air. PDNA: 254,000 children under 18 among 750,000 in urgent need. UNICEF (Sitrep #12) covers ~1 million affected children but gives no child death count.

value: not_found
finding: No study of property or land price effects found. Related evidence: Beira municipal plan (PDNA Annex 1) says 'approximately 70% of houses destroyed partially (63.506 units) or totally (23.833 units)' with 'The biggest destruction ... in the poorest neighborhoods'. PDNA warns 'Relocated families are at risk of losing access to their land', especially female-headed households. In Mozambique land is state-owned (DUAT use rights) so a formal land-price market is limited.

value: ~1 million without power (20 Mar 2019); reconstruction 56% complete after 5+ years
finding: NASA Earth Observatory VIIRS night-lights (9 vs 24 March 2019) show Beira largely dark; 'As of March 20, an estimated 1 million people were without electricity' and 'Nearly all electricity and internet went out, except near the airport'. No published Idai-specific night-light recovery duration found (IOP 2025 global study does not report it). EDM estimated 'Two weeks to fully restore electricity to all Beira neighbourhoods' (Club of Mozambique). Rebuild: 56% of reconstruction programme after ~5.4 years (Aug 2024); >90% of infrastructure claimed by Nov 2025. PDNA projected GDP growth cut from 4.7% planned to 2.5% in 2019, assuming a 'fall of more than 60% of the productive capacity' in the central region.

value: USD 39 m wage income lost; USD 513 m agricultural losses; 715,378 ha crops flooded
finding: PDNA: 'Over USD 39 million in income was lost due to unemployment'; agriculture losses USD 512.6 m (largest loss sector) and industry & commerce losses USD 470.1 m; 715,378 ha of cultivated land flooded; '433,056 farming families require seed starter kits, equivalent to 2.1 million people'; 2,044 fishing vessels destroyed; 9,710 animal deaths; 'Food consumption of staples has been reduced by over 50%'; poverty rate 'may rise to 79% in affected areas, up from 64%'. Agriculture employs 71% of the labour force.

value: 1.37 million reached with food/vouchers (WFP, by ~April 2019); vouchers US$44/month to 100,000 people
finding: WFP (Country Brief April 2019): with local authorities and partners it 'assisted 1.37 million people in four disaster-affected provinces through in-kind food distributions and commodity vouchers', with 330,000 planned for value/commodity vouchers in Beira, Dondo and Nhamatanda. WFP-UNICEF joint voucher programme (Aug-Oct 2019): 100,000 people per month in Dondo and Nhamatanda, monthly voucher of 2,670 meticais (US$44). Government SME subsidy agreements: 600 enterprises, 475 million meticais (~US$7.4 m) (AIM 2025). PDNA: 1,359,159 individuals required emergency food assistance. No government cash-grant uptake rate found.

value: Insured share ~0 ('Almost nothing was insured')
finding: Munich Re: 'Overall losses came to US$ 2.3bn. Almost nothing was insured.' PDNA damage split: private damage USD 660.9 m (housing USD 410.5 m entirely private) vs public USD 748.9 m; private losses USD 1,205.8 m - implying most household losses were borne uninsured. No precise insured share or household insurance-coverage survey found.

value: Track/intensity forecast ~3 days ahead; 0 operational radars (Beira and Xai-Xai radars defunct); flood forecasting weak
finding: ISET-International (March 2020, 'Learning from Cyclone Idai and Cyclone Kenneth to Strengthen Early Warning Systems in Mozambique') reports that the landfall location and wind speeds were accurately known several days ahead via regional/global forecasting, and INAM projected track and intensity about 3 days before landfall; but it notes there was no working weather radar in Mozambique - per WMO, INAM's two radars installed in 2004 at Xai-Xai and Beira had not been operational for years - and flood forecasting and uptake were 'less successful'. RSMC La Reunion (Meteo France) had described Idai as 'extremely dangerous', especially if storm surge coincided with high tide (WMO). Note: ISET text accessed only through search excerpts (ReliefWeb page returned 403), so wording is paraphrased.

value: Buzi CLGRCs warned within hours via megaphones/whistles; community radios warned hourly for 36 hours
finding: Local Disaster Risk Management Committees (CLGRC) in Buzi, trained by a Munich Re Foundation project (2005-2012), 'spread the warning within a few hours with megaphones and whistles in their communities and helped particularly vulnerable people to reach the few safe places', then 'provided rescue and first aid measures'; a survivor from Chicumba: 'Without the committee I would not exist anymore.' Community radios in Sofala broadcast warnings 'every hour for 36 hours' before landfall (WFP USA); a municipal official said 'the warnings saved lives, and many of them.' Conversely, Beira mayor Simango said rural areas at risk were not warned.

value: Near-total power and internet loss in Beira at landfall; ~1 million without power; radios off air
finding: Community radio stations in Sofala (Radio Beira, Dondo, Aguia, Buzi, Nhamatanda) broadcast warnings 'until the power was cut and everything went black' and were then damaged (WFP USA). NASA: 'Nearly all electricity and internet went out, except near the airport'; ~1 million without electricity on 20 March; the storm also cut transmission lines carrying power to South Africa. PDNA: port of Beira 'paralyzed for a few days' and 'transportation and communications services were interrupted'; energy damage USD 133.5 m. IDEA: power outages later prevented biometric voter registration in affected rural areas.

value: 41% do not understand written Portuguese; 44% of women do not understand spoken Portuguese
finding: Translators without Borders survey (April 2019, Beira relocation sites): '41% of people do not understand written Portuguese, the main language of humanitarian communication'; 'local languages like Sena, Ndau, and Chwabo are the most widely used and understood languages'; '44% of women do not understand spoken Portuguese' and '65% of women of all ages ... do not understand written information in any language'; '33% of people surveyed ... lack the information they need ... in a language they understand'. PDNA: national illiteracy 39% (females 49%); 111,000 people with disabilities directly affected. IDEA noted no mechanism was used to tell voters polling stations had moved and recommended community radio. No study of the language of the pre-landfall warnings themselves found.

value: Beira radar restored April 2023; Freddy deaths 53 (early official) to ~200 (UNDRR) vs Idai 603
finding: Post-Idai changes: World Bank-supported Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Program (US$265 m) and a revised EWS in which INAM issues alerts and the Institute of Social Communication disseminates via '70 community radios and trained community brigades', plus SMS mass warnings (World Bank, Sept 2023); new meteorological radar inaugurated by President Nyusi in Beira in April 2023 (AfDB/WMO/INAM), under the Master Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction 2021-2030 (UNDRR). Outcome in Cyclone Freddy (Feb-Mar 2023): World Bank says 'the relatively low number of fatalities ... reflects the success of this approach'; Nyusi reported 53 deaths and nearly 50,000 displaced as of 15-16 March 2023 (VOA), versus 603 for Idai; later tallies of ~200 Freddy deaths in Mozambique reported by UNDRR (not independently verified here). International IDEA resubmitted its Electoral Risk Management tool, which the CNE agreed in principle to implement in 2022.

value: Regional PP vs national PSOE; no national emergency declared; 'si necesita mas recursos, que los pida' (2 Nov 2024)
finding: Split control: Generalitat Valenciana led by PP (Carlos Mazon, governing with Vox support) held emergency command (kept emergency at level 2, never requested national level 3); national government PSOE-led (Pedro Sanchez). Help flowed but blame became partisan: on 2 Nov Sanchez said 'si necesita mas recursos, que los pida', criticised as conditioning aid on regional requests; ministers denied the paraphrase. Government stresses the alert was a regional competence; Consell says state coordination/information (CHJ, AEMET) failed. UME requested only at 20:36 on 29 Oct; ~10,000 troops deployed from 2 Nov. PP+Vox-controlled Corts inquiry (2026) exonerated the Generalitat and shifted blame to the central government.

value: PP -6 pts, Vox +4.9 pts (Sept 2026 poll vs 2023)
finding: No regional election held yet (due by 27 June 2027, likely 23 May 2027). PP support fell in polls after the DANA; Mazon resigned 3 Nov 2025 and was replaced by PP's Juanfran Perez Llorca (invested 27 Nov 2025 with Vox support). Sept 2026 poll vs 2023 result: PP 35.7% -> 29.7%, Vox 12.6% -> 17.5%, Compromis 14.5% -> 17.1%, PSPV 28.7% -> 27.5%; PP+Vox still near majority, gains going to Vox. ~130,000 protested in Valencia on 9 Nov 2024 demanding Mazon's resignation.

value: Paiporta visit 3 Nov 2024 (5 days after); PM CECOPI visit 31 Oct
finding: Sanchez visited the CECOPI in Valencia on 31 Oct 2024. On 3 Nov 2024 King Felipe VI, Queen Letizia, Sanchez and Mazon visited Paiporta; crowds threw mud and objects shouting 'Murderers!' and 'Get out!'. Sanchez and Mazon were whisked away by security; the royals stayed about an hour talking to residents. Mazon was at a long lunch at El Ventorrillo restaurant on 29 Oct, leaving ~18:00 and arriving at CECOPI ~19:30 (per Wikipedia), a central controversy.

value: RDL 6/2024 within 7 days; EUR 16.6bn mobilised, EUR 9.09bn used by Jan 2026
finding: Generalitat raised the emergency to level 2 (regional command); level 3 (national interest) never declared. Council of Ministers on 5 Nov 2024 declared the area 'zona afectada gravemente por una emergencia de proteccion civil' and approved Real Decreto-ley 6/2024 (BOE 6 Nov): direct aid regardless of income, EUR 20,640-60,480 for damaged homes, up to EUR 72,000 for death/disability, EUR 5,000 flat to self-employed, up to EUR 5bn ICO-type guarantees; first package ~EUR 10.6bn. By 12 Jan 2026 the state had mobilised EUR 16.6bn and used EUR 9.09bn (EUR 7.61bn paid in aid and subsidies). Follow-up RDL 12/2025 (28 Oct 2025).

value: Metro ~8 months; Mazon resigned after 1 year
finding: Metrovalencia lines through Horta Sud closed from 29 Oct 2024; EUR 130m reconstruction, Torrent stations back in service end of June 2025 (~8 months). CV-33 partially reopened 12-13 Nov 2024; >EUR 28m for CV-403/CV-36/CV-33. EUR 438.6m for water-cycle infrastructure by Jan 2026. 232 km of rail/road links needed repair. Political fallout: Mazon resigned as president 3 Nov 2025 (kept seat/immunity); ex-Emergencies councillor Salome Pradas and ex-secretary Emilio Argueso investigated for negligent homicide.

value: 57 health centres affected; 29 closed initially; 53/57 reopened by mid-Nov
finding: Initially 29 health centres/consultorios closed and operations cancelled (hospitals limited to emergencies); in total 57 primary-care centres affected, 53 reopened by mid-Nov 2024; Catarroja, Aldaia, Alaquas and Picanya centres stayed closed longer. Extraordinary care points set up. Savia nursing home Paiporta flooded (6 residents died); 95 residents relocated; affected residences housed 8,198 dependent people.

value: 1 pregnant victim (unborn child counted as victim 229); population birth outcomes not found
finding: Janine Mercado Rodriguez, a Bolivian woman 8 months pregnant, died; in June 2025 the Catarroja judge counted her unborn child as victim no. 229 (Civil Registry rule for deaths after 6 months' gestation). No systematic data found on births, prematurity or maternal service disruption.

value: >=3 leptospirosis cases; no major outbreak
finding: Ministry of Health and Conselleria de Sanitat ran daily epidemiological surveillance from 5 Nov 2024. At least 3 confirmed human leptospirosis cases reported in Nov 2024 (some earlier suspected cases tested negative). Internists (FESEMI) describe 'an exceptional epidemiological scenario' with unusual wound infections and a rise in bacterial gastroenteritis; an opinion piece in Gaceta Medica cites ~20% rise in waterborne disease cases (not an official figure). No large outbreak reported.

value: 2,227 displaced (Dec 2024); PTSD +147%, anxiety +63%
finding: Dec 2024: 2,227 people still out of their homes; 1,698 homes uninhabitable; 126 in Generalitat shelters (most displaced stayed with family/friends). Generalitat rent aid up to EUR 800/month for those forced out. Mental health: EAE Business School analysis reported PTSD cases +147% and anxiety diagnoses +63% in affected municipalities; Ministry of Health/ISCIII/Conselleria launched a 3-year mental-health surveillance study (Jan 2026).

value: 9 children; most deaths 19:00-20:00, before 20:11 alert
finding: Nine minors among the dead in Valencia (7 aged 10 or under, 2 aged 11-17); nearly half of victims aged 70+. Deaths concentrated in the evening, mostly between ~19:00 and 20:00 as the Poyo flood wave hit Horta Sud, i.e. before the 20:11 ES-Alert. Court summary: the alert came 'cuando ya se habian producido la mayoria de las muertes'.

value: Rents +5.76%; sale prices +4% (Horta Sud) to +17%
finding: Prices ROSE in affected zones due to reduced supply and relocation demand: Valencia Plaza reports +17% sale and +5% rent; Gloval study (Oct 2024-Jan 2025) found sale prices in l'Horta Sud +4% vs ~2% rest of province (Albal, Massanassa ~10%); rents in affected municipalities +5.76% in a year to EUR 12.28/m2/month, ~20% in Alzira and Catarroja. >92,500 properties in Horta Sud (50% of stock) affected.

value: Spending normal in ~1 month; commerce 8 months; small firms still -10% at 1 year
finding: CaixaBank Research (card data): resident spending fell 47% in the first week (82% for low-income vs 40% high-income households) and normalised within a month; business turnover fell 83% and took 8 months to align with national pace; small firms fell 98% and remained >10% below year-earlier levels after one year, while large firms recovered by Sept 2025. Nighttime-light change maps showed activity halts in industrial zones (Pista de Silla, Riba-roja, Aldaia, Quart). Media report ~85% of industrial firms reopened after one year; ~70% of urban shops operating.

value: 33,736 workers on ERTE; 92.4% returned by mid-2025
finding: Early Dec 2024: 2,882 companies had 30,417 workers on force-majeure ERTE (100% social-security exemption) and ~4,000 self-employed on cessation-of-activity benefit; in total 33,736 workers placed on DANA ERTEs, 92.4% back at work by June 2025. Social Security DANA measures protected >85,000 people in the first month. Ministry reports EUR 44.0m ERTE payments by Jan 2026.

value: 41,678 housing aid applications, EUR 249.8m paid; 26,943 firms/self-employed aided
finding: Government data 12 Jan 2026: housing/household-goods/death aid EUR 249.8m paid across 41,678 registered applications (33,044 resolved favourably per earlier tally); Plan Reinicia Auto+ 43,155 applications, EUR 208.6m; direct aid EUR 342.1m to 16,007 self-employed and 10,936 companies; EUR 76.9m to 9,136 farmers; employment plan 3,122 hires in 74 municipalities. Generalitat flat EUR 6,000 per damaged home. Irregular migrants (Oxfam est. 28,000-41,000) initially excluded; one-year regularisation for ~25,000.

value: EUR 4.484bn paid on 212,533 claims (June 2026); ~27% of damage
finding: Spain's Consorcio covers flood for any holder of a property/vehicle policy, so insured losses were paid via the public pool: 251,813 claims (95.4% in Valencia province), 212,533 paid, EUR 4.484bn by 5 June 2026; estimated total ~EUR 4.8bn - largest loss in its 70+ year history. Against EUR 17.8bn direct damage this is ~27% (computed). Uninsured gaps: public infrastructure, uninsured vehicles/homes, and irregular migrants in substandard housing; state aid (RDL 6/2024) paid regardless of income and complemented insurance.

value: Red warning 07:36, ~12.5 h before ES-Alert; forecast >200 mm vs 771.8 mm observed
finding: AEMET flagged a possible DANA 6 days ahead (23 Oct), issued its first red warning of 2024 in the Valencian Community at 07:31/07:36 on 29 Oct (forecasting >200 mm); observed up to 771.8 mm (Turis) - roughly four times the worst forecast. Experts: 'es imposible predecir si van a caer 700 l/m2 en seis u ocho horas en una localizacion concreta'; red levels do not pinpoint where catastrophic flooding will occur. ~225 personal weather stations (7x denser than AEMET gauges) recorded 200-300 mm by early afternoon; several stopped 15:10-16:15 (power/flood). CHJ SAIH gauge data on the Poyo had a gap 16:13-18:43.

value: 112 calls 16:40; CHJ flow alert 18:43; no local warning to Horta Sud
finding: No siren or local flood-warning system reached downstream Horta Sud residents. Signals existed: 112 calls from the Poyo basin from 16:40; CHJ automatic SAIH rainfall alert 17:02 and flow alert 18:43 (1,686 m3/s, rising); regional forest firefighters monitoring the Poyo were withdrawn at 14:30. Paiporta local police watched the ravine and closed bridges but it was not raining in Paiporta; the mayor told the delegation around 19:00 that 'in Paiporta people are drowning'. Savia Paiporta nursing home: 'No les llego ningun aviso del agua'.

value: ~180,000 power customers; 250-300k mobile customers cut
finding: ~180,000 i-DE (Iberdrola) electricity customers lost supply in l'Horta Sud, Catadau-Carlet and Requena-Utiel-Bunol; restored 99-100% within ~72 h (Iberdrola). Telecom: ~220,000 fixed and 250,000-300,000 mobile customers affected; by 31 Oct only 45% fixed and 30% mobile restored. Forensic teams reported 'Telephone lines are down' on 30 Oct. Savia residence lost power shortly after water entered (~19:30). Personal weather stations went offline 15:10-16:15. Disability barometer attributes 37 deaths of people with disabilities to failed telecare (teleasistencia) services.

value: Spanish+Valencian only (no English); no 'go upstairs' instruction; 450 deaf people unreached
finding: ES-Alert at 20:11 sent in Spanish and Valencian: 'Provincia de Valencia. Por las fuertes lluvias y como medida preventiva se debe evitar cualquier tipo de desplazamiento en la provincia de Valencia. Esten atentos a futuros avisos a traves de este canal y de fuentes oficiales en Twitter GVA 112 y A Punt.' It did not tell people to go to upper floors (corrected at 20:57); a Spanish/English draft ('707') was not the one sent. Sound-based warnings were 'completamente ineficaces para las 450 personas sordas identificadas' in the worst-hit areas (Barometro de Catastrofes / Fundacion ONCE, CERMI CV). 53 deaths of people with disabilities; nearly half of all victims 70+. 17 foreign nationals died; 28,000-41,000 irregular migrants affected (Oxfam) with barriers to aid.

value: Preventive ES-Alerts on red warnings; national civil-protection plans April 2026; no unified protocol yet
finding: Generalitat now issues preventive ES-Alerts when a red warning is active (policy: send with red level), but was again criticised for a late 22:08 ES-Alert on 16-17 Sept 2026, over an hour into torrential rain; victims' association: 'No queremos otro 29-O'. National Council of Ministers (April 2026) approved civil-protection reform/four state plans (floods, extreme weather) making ES-Alert 'una pieza central' and allowing access restrictions, suspension of activities or preventive evacuations based on AEMET warnings. Opposition in Congress still seeks a unified alert protocol. CERMI/ONCE call for a mandatory inclusive emergency plan.

value: Aligned (R federal, R state, R county); declaration in 2 days; USAR deployment reportedly >72 hours
finding: Fully aligned Republican chain: Republican President (Trump), Republican Governor (Abbott), Republican Lt. Gov. (Patrick), and a Republican-run county. Alignment did not prevent federal friction: DHS Secretary Kristi Noem's rule requiring her personal sign-off on contracts/grants over $100,000 was reported by CNN to have delayed deployment of FEMA Urban Search and Rescue teams until Monday, 'more than 72 hours after the flooding began', and FEMA call-center contracts had lapsed so many calls went unanswered; DHS denied the delay mattered. The federal major disaster declaration was nevertheless granted within ~2 days (6 July 2025), and Trump and Abbott toured Kerrville together on 11 July.

value: Local turnover limited; county judge open seat (incumbent not running); EM coordinator retired March 2026
finding: No general election has yet tested the flood (Texas general election is November 2026). In the 3 March 2026 Republican primary, Kerr County Judge Rob Kelly did not run (he said he decided before the flood not to seek a third term); Tom Jones won the Republican nomination for county judge 6,483 to 3,643 over James 'Jack' Stewart. A Houston Chronicle one-year review reported Kerrville-area leaders 'remain unchanged'; Emergency Management Coordinator W.B. 'Dub' Thomas announced his retirement in March 2026. No statewide polling effect on Abbott attributable to the flood was found.

value: Presidential visit day 7 (11 July 2025)
finding: Governor Abbott issued a state disaster declaration on 4 July and visited Kerr County in the first days. President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump visited Kerrville on Friday 11 July 2025 (7 days after the flood) with Abbott, meeting responders at Louise Hays Park and holding a roundtable at the Hill Country Youth Event Center. Trump: "It's hard to believe the devastation - trees that are 100 years old just ripped out of the ground - I've never seen anything like it." Not in an election period (midterm/state elections Nov 2026).

value: Declaration day 2; 22% of Kerr IHP applicants eligible (Oct 2025); ~$37-39M individual aid; ~$33M emergency work
finding: Trump approved Major Disaster Declaration DR-4879-TX on 6 July 2025 (about 2 days after the flood), initially for Kerr County with Individual Assistance, later expanded (10 counties added 30 July). As of 11 Oct 2025 FEMA had referred only 46% of Kerr County's 3,228 IHP applications to the next stage; 704 (22%) were found eligible and 775 denied, versus a 39% historical approval rate across 170 disasters (2015-May 2024). FEMA had approved $37 million in IHP aid across Central Texas. By Jan 2026 FEMA told NPR it had provided more than $33 million for emergency work plus $39 million to cover uninsured losses. Contrast: the July 2026 flood waited six-plus weeks for a major declaration (Public Assistance only, $50.5M, approved ~2 Sept 2026; Individual Assistance undecided).

value: Water plant emergency; officials criticized but remained in office; criminal probe of camp (Sept 2026)
finding: Kerrville declared a water supply emergency after its water treatment plant (Nimitz Lake) was damaged; Hunt's water system required restoration with a boil-water order. Accountability: Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick publicly criticized County Judge Rob Kelly at a Kerrville legislative hearing; Sheriff Larry Leitha and EMC Dub Thomas acknowledged being asleep when the flood began. The joint legislative General Investigating Committee report (June 2026) focused on Camp Mystic failures. Kerr County raised property taxes to pay for recovery. Texas Rangers opened a criminal investigation of Camp Mystic (manslaughter, criminally negligent homicide etc.) with 14 search warrants in Sept 2026.

value: No closure; mass-casualty surge; $1.9M hospital grants
finding: No hospital closure found. Peterson Regional Medical Center (Kerrville) activated its emergency operations center at 6:30 a.m. on 4 July and handled its first-ever mass casualty event ("Truck after truck started coming through the ER"). Texas HHSC awarded over $1.9 million in emergency grants to rural hospitals in Kerrville and Llano to repair damage and equipment, provide staffing support and address operational issues.

value: not_found
finding: No data or studies on births, pregnancy or maternal outcomes found; only anecdotal news stories of pregnant residents evacuating.

value: No outbreak found; boil-water notice; Hep A/tetanus clinics
finding: No outbreak reported. Preventive measures only: boil-water notice for Hunt water system; Kerrville water supply emergency; Peterson Health and DSHS ran free Hepatitis A and tetanus vaccine clinics for first responders and volunteers because floodwater may carry sewage; warnings about Aeromonas wound infections.

value: 2,000+ structures damaged; projected ~8,000 PTSD cases in Kerr County
finding: No official displacement count found. More than 2,000 structures damaged in Kerr County. FEMA temporary housing assistance and nonprofit aid (Community Foundation of the Texas Hill Country raised ~$100M; Airbnb.org $1.6M housing fund). Mental health: SAMHSA Disaster Distress Helpline activated; 24/7 Central Texas Flooding Emotional Support Line (833-812-2480); Hill Country Hearts and a Hill Country Emotional Support Center in Kerrville still open in July 2026. A post-flood study projected PTSD cases in Kerr County growing to about 8,000 (reported by KSAT). Undocumented families reported fear of seeking aid and PTSD symptoms.

value: 39 children of 117 Kerr dead (33%); 27 at Camp Mystic; overnight holiday
finding: 39 of 117 identified Kerr County dead were children (under 18), youngest aged 1 (KSAT, 8 Aug 2025). At Camp Mystic, 25 girl campers, 2 teenage counselors and owner/director Dick Eastland died. Timing: overnight on the 4 July national holiday; NWS flash flood warning at 1:14 a.m., the camp director called for help around 3 a.m., and the river swept through communities 'before sunrise'. Holiday crowds at riverside camps and RV parks raised exposure: 40+ people died in two Kerr County RV campgrounds.

value: Appraisal loss > $240M
finding: Kerr Central Appraisal District reported lost property value may exceed $240 million from flood damage; Kerr County and Kerrville raised tax rates citing disaster costs and lost values (Kerrville raised again in 2026 after the second flood). Kerr ranks 8th among Texas counties for share of buildings in dangerous flood zones; about 1,300+ properties are in the 100-year floodplain. Repairs under 50% of structure value need no code upgrades. No peer-reviewed sale-price study found.

value: Partial rebuild at 12 months; set back by July 2026 flood
finding: No nightlights study found. At one year (July 2026): some businesses reopened (Crider's, Howdy's), some homes rebuilt, others (River Inn, expected 2028; Hunt Store) still closed; Camp Mystic shut and filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy (June 2026). Community Foundation CEO Austin Dickson: "We are not recovered. We are in recovery, and there is much more work to be done." Recovery was reset by the 16 July 2026 flood (384 Kerr homes destroyed or majorly damaged; 9 of 11 bridges damaged).

value: DUA offered; job-loss count not_found
finding: Disaster Unemployment Assistance under DR-4879 opened for workers and self-employed in Burnet, Kerr, Guadalupe, Kimble, McCulloch, Menard, San Saba, Tom Green, Travis and Williamson counties; deadline extended to 29 Sept 2025. No count of DUA claims or jobs lost found. Over 300 businesses required assistance (Texas Tribune). AccuWeather's $18-22B estimate includes tourism and commerce losses.

value: 22% of applicants eligible (Oct 2025); $37M FEMA IHP approved
finding: Kerr County: 3,228 FEMA IHP applications; as of 11 Oct 2025 1,479 (46%) reviewed, 704 eligible (22% of applicants), 775 denied, 1,749 not yet reviewed. Approval rate well below the 39% historical average. Private philanthropy filled gaps: Community Foundation of Texas Hill Country ~$100M raised, $11.9M distributed to local nonprofits by end of July; typical early family assistance $5,000. Undocumented families hesitated to apply for fear of immigration enforcement.

value: ~2.5% NFIP take-up; <5% in 100-year floodplain
finding: Only about 2.5% of Kerr County homeowners had flood insurance (national rate 6%). Fewer than 150 of nearly 3,000 residential properties in the FEMA 100-year floodplain were NFIP-insured on 4 July (<5%). Houston Chronicle: most Kerr homes hit had no flood insurance. FEMA said it provided $39 million to cover uninsured losses (Jan 2026). No NFIP claims totals for the event were found.

value: Warning lead time 106 min (Hunt) / 26 min (Kerrville) vs 65-min goal; 6 WFO vacancies
finding: NWS issued a flood watch on 3 July (1:18 p.m.) and a flash flood warning at 1:14 a.m. on 4 July, sent to phones via IPAWS. Commerce OIG (Report OIG-26-017-I, 9 Apr 2026): 'Although staffing vacancies existed at the WFO, staff asserted that the vacancies did not affect their ability to forecast, issue flood alerts, and provide support to Kerr County officials.' OIG lead times: about 106 minutes at Hunt but effectively 26 minutes at Kerrville, versus a 65-minute goal; forecasters' calls to the county EMC and sheriff went unanswered; no river gauges upstream of Hunt on the South Fork. Austin/San Antonio WFO had 6 vacancies including the warning coordination meteorologist. The forecast underpredicted rain: TDEM chief Nim Kidd said 'the amount of rain that fell in this specific location was never in any of those forecasts.' A preprint notes HRRR QPF displacement errors of ~100-150 km in warm-season convection.

value: No sirens; CodeRED ~90 min after request; no local IPAWS alert
finding: Kerr County had no outdoor sirens or dedicated flood warning system. Plans since 2016 (former commissioner Tom Moser) stalled over >$1M cost and failed grants; a $731,413 FEMA grant application (for $976,000 of upgrades) was denied by TDEM for lack of a current hazard mitigation plan; ARPA funds went unused. Downstream Comfort had sirens. The county's opt-in CodeRED system was slow: a volunteer firefighter asked at 4:22 a.m. "Is there any way we can send a CodeRED out to our Hunt residents asking them to find higher ground or stay home?"; alerts went out about 90 minutes later and some residents got them hours later. FEMA records show the county did not use IPAWS to send its own alerts to all phones during critical hours.

value: Power outage (thousands of customers); counselors without phones/radios
finding: Power outages hit thousands of Kerr County customers on 4 July, worst on the South Fork between Hunt and Ingram. Cell coverage along the upper Guadalupe was poor; the legislative report found Camp Mystic had taken counselors' cellphones without supplying radios, so leaders could not reach cabins. SB 1 (2025) now requires camps to keep redundant communications (e.g., dual broadband). No quantified telecom outage data found.

value: >25% Hispanic; Spanish info gaps reported; warning-language data not_found
finding: Hispanic/Latino people make up more than 25% of Kerr County's ~52,600 residents (CNN). Reports said help for Latino families was delayed partly by a lack of rescue and recovery information in Spanish, and undocumented families avoided FEMA over immigration fears ("I'm afraid people are afraid to come out and get supplies" - Lisa Weinstein, ESL teacher in Hunt). No analysis of warning-message language (Spanish WEA/CodeRED) was found.

value: Laws passed Sept 2025; $294M package; 6 state + ~100 private sirens; 2026 flood deaths fell to ~1-2
finding: Second special session (signed 5 Sept 2025): SB 1 'Heaven's 27 Camp Safety Act' and HB 1 (camps in floodplains need emergency plans, evacuation protocols, redundant communications; cabin location limits); SB 3 funding outdoor warning sirens in flash-flood-prone areas; SB 5 appropriated $294M from the Rainy Day Fund ($50M for sirens/gauges in July 4 counties, $200M FEMA match, $24M forecasting). Kerr County formed a Flood Warning System Project Team (Aug 2025). By July 2026: 6 state-funded sirens in Kerr County with ~28 more planned, plus 90-100+ privately funded River Sentry sirens along the Guadalupe. July 2026 test: in the 16-18 July 2026 flood, Kerr County sent 4 wireless emergency alerts, Kerrville 1, NWS 38; new sirens sounded; at least 2 died regionally (1 in Kerr per Texas Tribune). A resident: "Last year, we got no alarms. We had no idea what was going on. This year, very different." Gaps persisted in Uvalde County (no local WEAs recorded).
